bug_semantics: The unauthenticated front-store GET /images handler reads the attacker-controlled src query string (with a required numeric w), passes it unchanged to imageProcessor, and imageProcessor treats any value beginning http:// or https:// as external. In vulnerable revisions that branch calls the global fetch(src) with no destination allowlist or private/loopback/link-local rejection, so a remote caller can make the EverShop server issue blind HTTP(S) requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts (CWE-918).
flaw_origin: Atomic commit 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 ("Feat: Image component", The Nguyen, 2025-09-17) created both pages/frontStore/images/images.ts and services/imageProcessor.ts. It first wrote the query-to-processor flow, the scheme-only isExternalUrl check, and the vulnerable `const response = await fetch(src)` sink. Its immediate parent has neither file. Commit a839543becedb75324a16c38194eb4c64ba5f635, two minutes later, added route.json for GET /images and thereby made the already-written sink routable; it is the activation commit, not the first writer of the flawed sink. The BIC is therefore the smaller atomic first-writer 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143, not the later PR merge or a move/refactor/squash aggregate.
ai_marker: BIC commit-object check: `git cat-file -p 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143` shows author and committer `The Nguyen <6950941+treoden@users.noreply.github.com>` and the complete message `Feat: Image component`. The commit object has no Co-Authored-By trailer, no Generated-with trailer, no AI/tool marker, and no bot/agent identity.
evidence: Reproduce in the validated clone /home/hanqing/agents/ai-slop/.ai-slop/state/repos/evershopcommerce_evershop (prefix heavy commands with `numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1`). Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vp8w-wj4m-3r7j says unauthenticated GET /images, arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS src, affected <=2.1.0, and no patched version as of its 2026-01-05 publication; https://pages.dos-m0nk3y.com/blog/EverShop%202.1.0%20-%20Unauthenticated%20DoS/#server-side-request-forgery-ssrf-cve-2025-67427 quotes the same isExternalUrl and fetch(src) path. BIC: `git show --format=fuller --patch 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/images.ts packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts` shows both files added and raw fetch(src); `git log -L '/const response = await fetch(src)/,+1:packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts' 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143` traces that line to this commit, while `git log --all --reverse -S'fetch(src)' -- packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts` reports 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 as the addition and af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7 as its removal. Parent: `git ls-tree -r 753e8aeac5e7a9753731a8ad0f449c05cb2fa61e -- packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts` produces no output, directly proving the parent lacks both vulnerable files. Activation and attack path: `git show a839543becedb75324a16c38194eb4c64ba5f635 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/route.json` shows addition of `{methods:[GET], path:/images}`; `git show v2.1.0:packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/route.json` shows that public front-store route in the release; `git blame v2.1.0 -L 1,35 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/images.ts` assigns query.src and imageProcessor(src,...) to 5ed5ba319; and `git blame v2.1.0 -L 65,216 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts` assigns the scheme test and fetch(src) sink to 5ed5ba319. Fix: `git show --format=fuller --patch af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7 -- packages/evershop/src/lib/util/secureFetch.ts packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts` shows creation of a strict IMAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS-based undici wrapper and replacement of fetch(src) with secureFetch(src), closing arbitrary-host SSRF. Version boundary: `git tag --contains 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 --sort=version:refname` yields v2.1.0, v2.1.1, v2.1.2, v2.2.1 (so v2.0.1 is pre-BIC); `git tag --contains af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7 --sort=version:refname` yields only v2.2.1. Thus v2.1.0 was the first vulnerable tagged release, Git history also shows later v2.1.1 and v2.1.2 remained vulnerable despite the advisory's publication-time <=2.1.0 range, and v2.2.1 is the first tagged release containing the fix. Marker: `git cat-file -p 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143` gives the exact human author/committer and one-line message quoted in ai_marker, with no trailers.
reasoning: The causal defect is the first-written scheme-only external-URL branch plus unguarded fetch(src), not the later route activation, merge, refactor, or fix. Both -L and -S independently pin those lines to 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143; its parent directly lacks the files. The later atomic fix af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7 removes the raw fetch and requires an allowed host, and tag reachability establishes the release boundary. Under the BIC-only attribution rule, the BIC's human author/committer and marker-free commit message provide no commit-object AI evidence, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI. AI provenance on any later route, merge, refactor, or fix would be irrelevant even if present.
